extracted.intended_audience: PRSA members and public relations professionals (chapter-level and practicing communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: A code of ethics for public relations practitioners outlining core professional values and concrete provisions/guidelines governing communication, client relations, conflicts, confidentiality, and conduct. Intended to guide day-to-day decision-making and establish obligations and consequences for PRSA members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent. We provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core professional value: members should advance clients' interests while considering and serving the public interest by ensuring voices and facts are presented to support informed debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must prioritize accuracy and truth in all communications; honesty underpins trust with the public and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience. We advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education. We build mutual understanding, credibility, and relationships among a wide array of institutions and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should pursue ongoing professional development, apply their specialized skills responsibly, and contribute to the profession's knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain objectivity in counsel and accept responsibility for decisions and outcomes; avoid undue influence that compromises professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance duty to clients/employers with obligation to the public; loyalty does not excuse unethical behavior or concealment of harmful information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public. We respect all opinions and support the right of free expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat all stakeholders equitably, respect differing opinions, and uphold free expression while avoiding discriminatory or unfair tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve the integrity of the process of communication. Be honest and accurate in all communications. Act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the practitioner is responsible. Preserve the free flow of unprejudiced information when giving or receiving gifts by ensuring that gifts are nominal, legal, and infrequent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific obligations: maintain integrity of communications, correct errors quickly, and avoid gift practices that bias or appear to bias information flow (gifts should be nominal, legal, infrequent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow ethical hiring practices designed to respect free and open competition without deliberately undermining a competitor. Preserve intellectual property rights in the marketplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not engage in unethical hiring or competitive practices that deliberately sabotage competitors; respect and protect intellectual property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Be honest and accurate in all communications. Act promptly to correct erroneous communications for which the practitioner is responsible. Investigate the truthfulness and accuracy of information released on behalf of those represented. Reveal the sponsors for causes and interests represented. Disclose financial interest (such as stock ownership) in a client's organization. Avoid deceptive practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before releasing information, verify accuracy; fully disclose sponsors and financial interests that could influence messaging; avoid deceptive or misleading practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguard the confidences and privacy rights of present, former, and prospective clients and employees. Protect privileged, confidential, or insider information gained from a client or organization. Immediately advise an appropriate authority if a member discovers that confidential information is being divulged by an employee of a client company or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect sensitive and privileged information; take prompt action (notify appropriate authority) if confidential information is being improperly disclosed by client employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Act in the best interests of the client or employer, even subordinating the member's personal interests. Avoid actions and circumstances that may appear to compromise good business judgment or create a conflict between personal and professional interests. Disclose promptly any existing or potential conflict of interest to affected clients or organizations. Encourage clients and customers to determine if a conflict exists after notifying all affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively identify and disclose real or perceived conflicts; prioritize client/employer interests over personal gain and encourage client evaluation of disclosed conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that there is an obligation to protect and enhance the profession. Keep informed and educated about practices in the profession to ensure ethical conduct. Actively pursue personal professional development. Decline representation of clients or organizations that urge or require actions contrary to this Code. Accurately define what public relations activities can accomplish. Counsel subordinates in proper ethical decision making. Require that subordinates adhere to the ethical requirements of the Code. Report ethical violations, whether committed by PRSA members or not, to the appropriate authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must support the profession by staying educated, refusing unethical representation, setting accurate expectations about PR, mentoring subordinates on ethics, enforcing the Code within their teams, and reporting violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member Code of Ethics Pledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Pledge: To conduct myself professionally, with truth, accuracy, fairness, and responsibility to the public; to improve my individual competence and advance the knowledge and proficiency of the profession through continuing research and education; and to adhere to the articles of the Member Code of Ethics 2000 for the practice of public relations as adopted by the governing Assembly of the Public Relations Society of America. I understand and accept that there is a consequence for misconduct, up to and including membership revocation. And, I understand that those who have been or are sanctioned by a government agency or convicted in a court of law of an action that is in violation of this Code may be barred from membership or expelled from the Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members explicitly commit to conduct standards, ongoing competence-building, and adherence to the Code; acknowledges possible sanctions (membership revocation or expulsion) for misconduct or legal sanctions related to Code violations.
